The function $f(x)$ is defined and differentiable on $[-10,-2].$ The graph of ${f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ is shown above, where the areas of the regions between the graph and the $x$-axis are $7$ and $5$ respectively (from left to right). Find the minimum value of $f(x)$ on the interval $[-10,-2]$ given that $f(-10)=0.$

${f}_{\text{min}}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
According to the candidates' test, the minimum value of $f(x)$ on $[-10,-2]$ must occur at a critical point or an endpoint of the interval.

**Step 1**: Find the critical points:

We see that ${f}^{′}(x)$ is defined everywhere on $x\in (-10,-2),$ and ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ at $x=-6.$ Therefore, the candidates are $x=-10,-6,-2.$

**Step 2**: Compute the value of $f$ for each candidate using the fundamental theorem of calculus:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-10) & =0 \\ f(-6) & =f(-10)+{\int }_{-10}^{-6}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =0+7 \\  & =7 \\ f(-2) & =f(-10)+{\int }_{-10}^{-2}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =0+7-5 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Select the smallest value of $f$ from our candidates.

Comparing the values of $f$ found in step $2,$ we have

$$
{f}_{\text{min}}=min\{0,7,2\}=0.
$$

Therefore, the minimum value of $f$ is ${f}_{\text{min}}=0,$ and the value of $x$ that minimizes $f(x)$ is ${x}_{\text{min}}=-10.$
